title: CCD: global carbonate compensation depth evolution over the last 170 million years and its drivers
description: Workflow, derived data and figures reconstructing the global carbonate compensation depth (CCD) over the last 170 million years and testing its drivers. An area-weighted global CCD is synthesised from Atlantic, Pacific and Indian Ocean records on a single timescale (GTS2020), calibrated against long-term sea level by reduced-major-axis regression, extended to 170 Ma as a hybrid observed/sea-level curve, converted into global carbonate sediment thickness on a plate reconstruction, and used to drive a deep-Earth carbon degassing model. Includes the reconstructed CCD record, the ocean-basin area fractions, the carbonate volume and budget tables, the DSDP/ODP ground-truth comparison at 38 basement sites, the attribution of the CCD to sea level and to solid-Earth carbon fluxes, all figure and animation scripts, and the three supplementary datasets cited by the accompanying manuscript. The reconstructed carbonate sediment thickness grids (minimum, central and maximum sedimentation-rate scenarios), the paleobathymetry grids, the continental masks, the plate model and the rendered animations are archived separately on Zenodo and are not redistributed here, nor are the third-party seafloor-age, spreading-rate, sediment-thickness and crustal-carbon grids read by the carbon-cycle stage.
